report.source_text: Subsequent CT angiogram confirmed a pulmonary sling, with the left pulmonary artery arising from the distal right pulmonary artery and wrapping around the distal trachea (Fig. 2). Left proximal mainstem bronchus obstruction, consistent with left-sided air trapping, was observed. Moderate-sized patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) and a notable patent foramen ovale (PFO) were present. Furthermore, a right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus) was identified (Fig. 3).

clinician.final_diagnosis: left pulmonary arterial sling with an associated right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-week-old female presented with respiratory distress and weight loss. Initial echocardiogram revealed a left pulmonary arterial sling, prominent patent foramen ovale, and a moderate size patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). A subsequent CT angiogram confirmed the pulmonary sling, identified left proximal mainstem bronchus obstruction, and also identified a right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus). At 7-months-old, the patient underwent surgical repair for the left pulmonary artery sling and PDA. Postoperatively, she developed left pulmonary artery stenosis, which was treated with balloon angioplasty, but recurrent stenosis occurred due to significant left pulmonary artery hypoplasia.

CT angiogram identified a right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus).
CT angiogram identified left proximal mainstem bronchus obstruction, consistent with left-sided air trapping.

At 7-months-old, the patient underwent left pulmonary artery sling and PDA repair with re-implantation of the left pulmonary artery into the main pulmonary artery anterior to the trachea and PDA division/ligation.

Patient developed postoperative left pulmonary artery stenosis and underwent successful balloon angioplasty, but developed recurrent left pulmonary artery stenosis due to significant left pulmonary artery hypoplasia.
